name: Lois Sportswear, U.S.A., Inc. v. Levi Strauss & Co.
summary: The Second Circuit held that trademark infringement can be based on confusion that occurs after a sale is completed, protecting the mark owner's interest in maintaining the reputation and distinctiveness of its brand.
significance: One of the foundational Second Circuit cases recognizing post-sale confusion as a valid theory of trademark infringement, cited in the debate over whether that doctrine was correctly applied below.
